# Selling part of a holding bought at a rate with three decimals.
#
# 100.00 USD at 1.405 CAD/USD costs 140.50 CAD — a whole number of cents, so
# the basis is booked as stated and its cost per unit is the 1.405 this file
# wrote. Selling 33.00 USD of it costs 33 × 1.405 = 46.365 CAD, which is half
# a cent, and money rounds away from zero: the sale is worth 46.37.
#
# So a file has one figure it may state for that split, and 46.36 is not it.
# The check allowed either while it forgave half a cent; the expected figure
# is rounded the engine's way and compared exactly now.
#
# This file is the purchase only. The sale that measures against it is
# `fx_sell_part_of_a_lot_at_its_basis.txt`, which names the basis this one
# opens.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_a_sale_is_valued_at_its_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:FX Gain
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

2026-01-10 * "Buy 100 USD at 1.405"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.405"
		value: "140.50"
	Assets:Bank -140.50 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-140.50"
